title.narrative: From Awareness to Action: Establishing a Policy and Governance Framework for the Protection and Restoration of Harare's Wetlands

description.narrative:
In July 2025, Zimbabwe hosted the 15th Ramsar COP and assumed its presidency for a three-year term, committing on a global platform to strengthening wetland protection at home and worldwide. This major international event also came at a time of heightened public concern over growing water challenges and environmental destruction nationally, but especially in Harare which is in a water crisis, and where wetlands remain under constant threat as the city rapidly grows and the climate changes.
Altogether, this has created unprecedented political will from Government of Zimbabwe especially the key Ministry of Environment and associated agencies which face accusations of negligence or even complicity in inappropriate developments over the years.
With support from the Netherlands Embassy in 2024–2025, BirdLife Zimbabwe (BLZ) built on its long-standing wetland conservation work to substantially elevate awareness and concern across public, private, and government sectors. During this period, BLZ collaborated closely with key ministries, parliament, government agencies, and the City of Harare to strengthen understanding of wetlands’ vital role in securing the city’s water supply and to outline and promote the urgent policy reforms needed to ensure their long-term protection while also supporting strong participation of CSOs at COP15, and providing progressive policy advice to Government of Zimbabwe during that event.
Building on these results, this project seeks to turn awareness into action by strengthening legal and institutional frameworks, empowering local authorities and communities to manage and restore wetlands, and engaging the private sector to promote responsible investment and sustainable urban development.
Key activities include supporting revisions to wetland-related policies and regulations, developing a concept for a dedicated Wetlands Act to domesticate Ramsar commitments, integrating wetland protection into Harare’s masterplan, and creating a framework for community–government management agreements. Media campaigns and targeted engagement with developers, financiers and EIA practitioners will help shift practice toward safeguarding wetlands as critical to water management.
This initiative seeks to leverage Zimbabwe’s Ramsar presidency and Harare's water crisis to precipitate stronger legislation and governance, improved management of Harare’s wetlands, and greater accountability among public, private, and community actors with regards to safeguarding ecosystems essential to the city’s water security.
